_comment: Arm (c2) postcondition derivations. Written by a human applying derivation-rules.md 'c2', in a step of its own, BEFORE the first judge call (PREREGISTRATION.md 7.1 construction order). This file is hashed into every run manifest, so a derivation added after a judge verdict is visible is mechanically detectable and is an amendment under rule 2 rather than a quiet edit.
_keying: Entries are keyed by request signature (c2_postcond.request_signature: sha256 of the whitespace-normalised, lower-cased task prompt, first 16 hex). Keyed by the request, not by a task identifier, so the file stays a rule application and cannot become a per-task answer key. Each entry repeats the request text verbatim; c2_postcond.audit_all re-hashes it and rejects any entry whose text does not hash to its own key.
_coverage: The derivation procedure was applied to EVERY request in the battery in one pass, including the ones it must refuse. Deriving only where a derivation was expected to succeed would select the numerator of MD_c2, so refusals are recorded as first-class entries with their reason rather than left absent.
_forbidden: No expected value, no per-task tolerance, no task identifier, and no family name may appear in this file. c2_postcond.validate_derivation enforces all four mechanically: every literal a pipeline compares against must be declared in `literals` with a source, and a `prompt`-sourced literal must actually occur in the request text. An expected value does not occur in the text of the request that produced it.
_precision: Every entry names the rung of derivation-rules.md's precision ladder its comparison rests on. Rung P1 (schema-declared precision) is EMPTY ON THIS TARGET: groundtruth/openapi.json contains no multipleOf and no numeric format in any of its 243 component schemas. See PREREGISTRATION.md Amendment B2.
